title: A 38.1Mb/mm2 SRAM in a 2nm-CMOS-Nanosheet Technology for High-Density and Energy-Efficient Compute
problem: Scaling SRAM bit-cell area at advanced nodes faces diminishing returns; peripheral circuits dominate area overhead, and maintaining reliability at reduced cell voltage becomes challenging.
motivation: Embedded memories are critical SoC bottlenecks for on-chip cache and compute buffers; higher SRAM density reduces memory footprint, enabling larger compute arrays and more efficient power delivery.
method: Design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) leveraging 2nm nanosheet technology's improved on/off-current ratio to increase BL loading capacity by 2x, allowing denser memory bit arrays per peripheral circuit. Special logic rules and floor-planning techniques optimize both cell and peripheral area while maintaining reliability margins.
key_novelty: First production-grade SRAM design exploiting nanosheet FET's current-ratio advantages to achieve 2x BL loading increase, coupled with area-optimized peripheral logic and DTCO floor-planning.
contributions: 2x increase in maximum bitline loading by leveraging nanosheet technology on/off-current ratio
Area-optimized peripheral logic using special design rules for advanced nodes
Comprehensive DTCO methodology spanning cell, macro-architecture, design-assist, and floor-planning
38.1 Mb/mm² density demonstrating advanced-node scaling achievement
baselines: conventional SRAM at prior technology nodes
limitations: Specific power, access time, and reliability metrics (SRAM margins, yield) not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: High-density SRAM using nanosheet DTCO for advanced-node embedding
